factors.name: Pace & Transition
factors.desc: How often possessions end in early-clock / transition shots (after steals, rebounds and even made baskets) versus long, late-clock half-court possessions.

factors.name: Ball Movement
factors.desc: Share of made baskets that are assisted, at the rim, from mid-range and from three. Low = isolation / one-on-one creation.

factors.name: Shot Diet
factors.desc: Where the jump shots come from: the 3-point line or 2-point jumpers. Three-heavy teams also tend to crash the glass less.

factors.name: Foul Pressure
factors.desc: How often the offense forces defensive fouls and gets to the line, including early in the shot clock.

factors.name: Rim Pressure
factors.desc: Share of shots at the rim plus putback frequency, versus jump shots.

factors.name: Risk Profile
factors.desc: Turnovers (especially live-ball) plus offensive rebounding: an aggressive, chaotic offense versus a careful one.

archetypes.name: Run-and-Gun
archetypes.desc: The fastest offenses in the league: early-clock shots after steals, rebounds and even made baskets, with the ball moving.

archetypes.name: Patient Precision
archetypes.desc: Slow, low-turnover half-court offense that works the clock for a good jump shot. Low variance, with few empty possessions.

archetypes.name: Threes & Free Throws
archetypes.desc: Lives at the three-point line and the free-throw line and skips the mid-range.

archetypes.name: Grind & Crash
archetypes.desc: Slower half-court offense built on two-point shots, inside and from mid-range, that crashes the offensive glass.

factors.name: Transition Defense
factors.desc: How often opponents get early-clock transition shots, after rebounds, makes or steals.

factors.name: Zone Signature
factors.desc: Share of opponents' baskets that are assisted. Zones give up passes and assisted shots; aggressive man defenses force one-on-one play. The clearest zone fingerprint.

factors.name: Foul Tendency
factors.desc: Defensive fouls and opponent free-throw rate, including reach-in fouls early in the clock.

factors.name: Mid-Range Funnel
factors.desc: Share of opponent shots that are 2-point jumpers. Drop coverage and help-heavy schemes concede the mid-range to protect the rim and arc.

factors.name: Rim vs. Arc
factors.low: Runs shooters off, concedes the rim
factors.desc: Which shots the defense gives up: threes (pack-line style) or rim attempts (extended perimeter coverage).

archetypes.name: Conservative Pack-Line
archetypes.desc: The most common defense. Sits back, protects the paint and concedes threes, forcing few turnovers and allowing few mid-range jumpers.

archetypes.name: Zone
archetypes.desc: The unmistakable zone fingerprint: opponents' baskets are heavily assisted, with lots of passing around the perimeter.

archetypes.name: Denial Man-to-Man
archetypes.desc: Pressures the ball and denies passes: forces turnovers, allows few assisted looks, and makes opponents work deep into the shot clock.

archetypes.name: Steady Middle
archetypes.desc: No strong lean either way: a little more physical than average, and funnels a few more shots to mid-range.

factors.name: Rotation Depth
factors.desc: Effective rotation size, bench minutes and how spread minutes are across lineups.

factors.name: Who Drives It
factors.desc: Share of usage and rebounding by guards versus forwards and centers.

factors.name: Post Player Type
factors.desc: Minutes to back-to-the-basket posts versus wings and stretch forwards who shoot threes.

factors.name: Star Usage
factors.desc: How concentrated usage is in the top player.

archetypes.name: Small-Ball Guards
archetypes.desc: Guards carry the usage and the rebounding; undersized, with wings instead of traditional bigs.

archetypes.name: Tight Rotation
archetypes.desc: Leans on a short rotation, with scoring spread around instead of one star.

archetypes.name: Star System
archetypes.desc: Offense funneled through one high-usage player.

archetypes.name: Forward-Led Positionless
archetypes.desc: Forwards run the offense; skilled, versatile bigs and wings with few traditional centers.
